subject: ventures/wall-framing-takeoff
auditor: agent session (Claude), see run record prompts/runs/ for 2026-11-28 quality/0
professional: a lead framer / framing estimator for residential wood-frame work, and a licensed plumber who sizes domestic water supply. The framer checks header, jack and cripple lengths and counts first; the plumber checks that every branch carries at least the fixture it feeds and that the worst fixture keeps its minimum pressure.

evidence.correctness: Ran the engines with probes (scratchpad c1.mjs and node -e calls). r5's high defect is closed: the 300 ft 1/2 in PEX shower branch (p 0.0093, 40 psi) now carries 2.5 gpm, is upsized to 3/4 in, loses 5.374 psi and ends at 34.63 psi; my own Swamee-Jain/Darcy at 60 F (bore 0.681 in, Re 10,269) gives 5.33 psi (0.8% apart). A lone toilet at p 0.01 is sized for its 3 gpm. Example-house velocities match Q/A by hand (12.2 gpm in 1.025 in bore: 4.746 ft/s; 5 gpm in 0.545 in: 6.880 ft/s), and the page's 8.1 ft/s for 12.2 gpm in 3/4 in copper L (bore 0.785) recomputes. Framing on a 144 in wall with a 38.5 x 82.5 door and a 2x10 header, 8 ft precuts: header 41.5 (RO + 2 jacks), jacks 81 (82.5 - 1.5 plate), top cripples 2.375 (97.125 wall - 3 top plates - 91.75), bottom plate cut 48 + 57.5, 7 commons + 3 cripples on the 16 in layout. A 36.5 x 48.5 window under a 2x8: header 39.5, top cripples 4.375, sill 36.5, bottom cripples 31 (34 RO bottom - sill - plate) at both sill ends plus layout. All match hand arithmetic.
evidence.completeness: Full suite runs green; the water-supply page, framing engine and electrical module do what README rows 71-72 and the ROADMAP say, with the listed gaps (no CLI flag for supply sizing, no header span table) stated. 4 of the 8 r5 defects are still open (velocity split, header table, gable loop, and partly the README count before this PR).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in ventures/wall-framing-takeoff: 1284 tests, 1283 pass, 1 skipped, 0 fail, 19 s. Three seeded mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on the full suite: dropping the low-p floor (supplysize.mjs:278) is caught (1 fail); jack = header height - 2 plates (engine.mjs:402) is caught (5 fail, r5: 2); dropping the per-face cable-hole multiplier (electrical.mjs:137) SURVIVED, as in r5. This PR adds a hand-counted interior-wall test that catches it (re-run: caught).
evidence.craft: engine.mjs is 1,737 lines (r5 1,718) and layoutGable (engine.mjs:668) still repeats layoutWall's opening loop. validateSupply ignores unknown segment keys: supplysize.test.mjs:207 passes maxSize: "1/2", which is not a field, so the branch comes out 3/4 in and the test's author believed it was capped. The fix itself (supplysize.mjs:272-278) is small, commented and cites the audit.
evidence.claims: README test count was stale again (1,213 / 144 files vs 1,284 / 151 today); corrected in this PR. The page's FAQ figures (27.2 gpm all-on, 12.2 gpm design, 8.1 ft/s in 3/4 L) recompute. The page states it is not IPC/UPC fixture-unit sizing, carries the no-warranty disclaimer, and tells the user to have a licensed plumber size the system. The README's 'within 15% of Hazen-Williams C=150' holds at the five tested points; at 2.5 gpm in 3/4 in PEX the ratio is 1.20, where Darcy is the better model at Re near 10,000, so not a defect.
evidence.fitness: A framer can type a wall with door and window and get a cut list whose lengths a crew can cut from (checked above); a plumber gets per-branch sizes and residual pressures, with the stated caveat that inspectors check the code fixture-unit tables. The free edition is the front door to the paid residential takeoff (bet #6, ventures/residential-takeoff).
evidence.domain: Framing practice (full-length jacks from plate to header, header = RO + 3 in, cripples on layout plus one at each sill end) matches common residential framing. Water sizing follows Hunter's 1940 probabilistic method computed exactly, with a floor at one fixture's flow as Hunter's curve and IPC Table E103.3(3) have. It departs from practice in one velocity for hot and cold (copper hot water is usually held near 5 ft/s) and in leaving header sizing wholly to the user's table.

verdict: Re-audit of r5 after PR 17614. The high defect is closed: a rarely used fixture's branch now carries that fixture's flow (2.5 gpm, 5.374 psi over 300 ft of 3/4 in PEX, 0.8% from my own Darcy/Swamee-Jain), the seeded removal of the floor is caught, and the jack guard grew from 2 failing tests to 5. Six framing and plumbing outputs recompute by hand. Of r5's 8 defects, 3 are closed, 1 partial (the README count, fixed and drifted again) and 4 open on arrival; the per-face cable-hole mutant still survived the 1284-test suite, and this PR adds the hand-counted test that catches it. With correctness back to 3 the subject meets the bar again (r5: missed it); craft stays 2 (1,737-line engine, duplicated gable loop, unknown keys silently ignored). Scores are before this PR's fixes.
